refined.title: Your refined settings (attempt {{n}})
refined.text: These values were adjusted after your last take. When you're done, record again at {{dist}}.
refined.communityText: Someone shared these values on GitHub. Every room and voice is different, so when you're done, record again at {{dist}} to check they work for you.

entry.stepByStep: Set it up step by step

head.lead: We show you where to click and what to type, with the values from your own check.

empty.title: Nothing to set up yet
empty.text: The guide uses the settings from your check. Do the check first (it takes a few minutes), then come back here.

host.question: What do you use for your mic?
host.hint: We remember your answer. You can change it any time.

wavelink.name: Elgato Wave Link
wavelink.text: The Elgato app that mixes your mic and adds effects to it.

obs.name: OBS Studio
obs.text: You stream or record videos with OBS.

apps.name: Discord, Teams or Zoom only
apps.text: You just talk in calls and use no other audio app.

nvidia.name: NVIDIA Broadcast
nvidia.text: NVIDIA's app that removes background noise (needs an RTX graphics card).

unsure.title: How to choose
unsure.text: The app you pick is where the effects run. Take the first one that fits you:
unsure.wavelink: Your mic is plugged into an Elgato device (like a Wave XLR), or you already have Wave Link: use Wave Link.
unsure.obs: You stream or record videos: use OBS Studio.
unsure.apps: You only talk in calls: use the settings inside Discord, Teams or Zoom.

nav.allDone: All done. Record the take with effects to hear the difference.

test.title: Test it
test.a2: Record the last take, the one with your effects.
test.a3: Look at the score before and after.
test.dist: Record at the same distance as your best take: {{dist}}.

wl.markApplied: Finished setting everything up? Tell us, so we can check your next take against these settings.

effects.title: Open your mic's effects
effects.lead: Only the effects we picked should be on. Other effects would fight with them.
effects.a1: Open Wave Link and click your mic.
effects.deess: Keep Elgato De-Esser on, set lightly: it softens sharp S sounds.

add.title: Add {{plugin}}
add.a1: If {{plugin}} is not in the list, click "+ Add effect" and pick "{{plugin}} (ReaPlugs Edition)".
add.a2: Drag it to place {{n}} in the list.
add.a3: Click its sliders icon to open its window.

setup.title: ReaFIR: pick the mode
setup.lead: ReaFIR removes the steady sound of your room, like fans or hiss.

profile.title: ReaFIR: let it learn your room
profile.lead: ReaFIR needs to hear the room alone, without your voice. Get ready to stay quiet for about 3 seconds.
profile.a3: Count to 3 in your head, still silent.

reduce.title: ReaFIR: turn the room down
reduce.lead: The curve now shows your room. Lowering it removes that sound.
reduce.a1: Drag the whole curve down a little: about {{amount}}.
reduce.a2: Talk and listen. Stop at the first watery or robotic sound.
reduce.a3: If it never sounds clean, use an AI noise remover instead (Elgato Noise Removal or NVIDIA Broadcast).

eq.title: ReaEQ: band {{n}} of {{total}}
eq.notch: It is a narrow cut for a fan or machine tone.
eq.tabs: First, use Add band or Remove band until the tabs go from 1 to {{total}}.

eqFlat.title: ReaEQ: nothing to change
eqFlat.lead: Your voice already sounds natural. Leave ReaEQ flat: remove any bands it has with Remove band, or switch ReaEQ off.

comp.title: ReaComp: even out your volume
comp.lead: It turns loud moments down, so your quiet and loud words end up closer.
comp.afterNr: After noise removal your voice may get quieter: raise Wet by the same amount (the results show how much).

gate.title: ReaGate: quiet the pauses
gate.lead: It closes when you stop talking, so the room is not heard between your words.
gate.leadNoisy: Set gently: it only lowers the room a little between words, so quiet words are never cut.

lowcut.title: Turn on the low cut
lowcut.lead: The low cut removes rumble (desk bumps, traffic) before it reaches the effects.
lowcut.a1: In Wave Link, click your mic and find the Lowcut switch (with the mic settings, not in Effects).

ai.title: Try AI noise removal first
ai.lead: Your voice is close to the noise of your room. Here an AI noise remover usually keeps your voice cleaner than ReaFIR. Try one of these first.
ai.skip: Talk and listen. If it sounds clean, skip ReaFIR.

elgato.title: Option 1: Elgato Noise Removal (in Wave Link)
elgato.a1: In Wave Link → your mic → Effects, switch on Elgato Noise Removal.
elgato.a2: Drag it to the top, so it comes first.

nvidia.title: Option 2: NVIDIA Broadcast (RTX graphics cards)
nvidia.a1: Open NVIDIA Broadcast → Microphone, pick your mic as Source and switch on Noise Removal.
nvidia.a2: In Wave Link and in your apps, choose "Microphone (NVIDIA Broadcast)" as the mic.

reafir.title: Use ReaFIR instead
reafir.lead: If neither sounds clean, or you can't use them: switch off Elgato Noise Removal and the Noise Removal in NVIDIA Broadcast, then follow the ReaFIR steps.

chosen.elgato: The next steps skip ReaFIR. Elgato Noise Removal stays on, first in the list.
chosen.nvidia: The next steps skip ReaFIR. Keep Elgato Noise Removal off: use only one noise remover.
chosen.reafir: The next steps set up ReaFIR.

listen.title: Listen check
listen.lead: Talk for 10 seconds and play it back: if words get cut or sound underwater, turn noise removal down.

auto.title: Apply automatically instead
auto.text: If you are comfortable with a terminal, a small script can write these values into Wave Link for you.
auto.a2: Download the settings file ("Download .json" in the suggested settings of your results).
auto.a4: It saves a backup of your Wave Link settings first.
auto.a5: ReaFIR still has to be set up by hand: the script cannot write its noise profile.

open.title: Open your mic's filters
open.lead: OBS has its own filters. We map your values onto them.
open.a1: In OBS, find your mic in the Audio Mixer.
open.a3: Add each filter of the next steps with the + button, in that order.

noise.title: Noise Suppression
noise.lead: It removes the steady sound of your room.
noise.vst: Prefer ReaFIR? Add "VST 2.x Plug-in" instead, pick ReaFIR and follow the ReaFIR steps of the Wave Link guide.

expander.title: Expander
expander.lead: A gentle expander lowers the room between words without cutting quiet words.

gate.title: Noise Gate
gate.lead: A noise gate closes when you stop talking, so the room is not heard between your words.

eq.title: 3-Band EQ
eq.lead: This EQ has three controls: low (below {{low}}), mid, and high (above {{high}}). These values come close to your ReaEQ settings.
eq.notches: Your settings also cut fan or machine tones, which 3-Band EQ cannot do. For those, add "VST 2.x Plug-in" → ReaEQ instead and type the values from the Wave Link guide.
eq.vst: For the exact result, add "VST 2.x Plug-in" → ReaEQ instead and type the values from the Wave Link guide.

comp.title: Compressor
comp.lead: It turns loud moments down, so your quiet and loud words end up closer.

limiter.title: Limiter
limiter.lead: A safety net: it never lets your voice go over the top.

install.title: Install NVIDIA Broadcast
install.lead: It needs an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.
install.a1: Download NVIDIA Broadcast from NVIDIA's website and install it.
install.a2: Open it and go to the Microphone tab.

enable.title: Turn on Noise Removal
enable.lead: It removes the room and keeps your voice.
enable.a2: Choose the effect "Noise Removal" and switch it on.
enable.a3: Keep the strength where it is. Raise it only if the room is still heard.

use.title: Use it in your apps
use.lead: Your apps must listen to NVIDIA Broadcast, not to the mic directly.
use.a1: In Discord, Teams, Zoom or OBS, pick "Microphone (NVIDIA Broadcast)" as your mic.
use.a2: Switch off the app's own noise suppression, so the two do not fight.

noise.title: Switch on noise suppression
noise.lead: Every call app can remove room noise. Turn it on:
noise.discord: Discord: User Settings → Voice & Video → Noise Suppression.
noise.zoom: Zoom: Settings → Audio → Suppress background noise.

echo.title: Echo cancellation: only with speakers
echo.lead: Using speakers? Leave echo cancellation on, so people don't hear themselves. Using headphones? You can turn it off: your voice sounds more natural.
echo.discord: Discord: User Settings → Voice & Video → Echo Cancellation.

gain.title: Automatic volume
gain.ok: Your volume is fine. Turn the automatic volume off, so the app doesn't keep changing it.
gain.fix: First fix your mic's input volume (see your results). Then turn the automatic volume off.
gain.discord: Discord: User Settings → Voice & Video → Automatic Gain Control.
gain.zoom: Zoom: Settings → Audio → Automatically adjust microphone volume.

free.title: Free things that help most
free.lead: These cost nothing and help in any app:
free.none: Nothing else needed: your mic setup is already in good shape.
